user_prompt:
Using line segment AO below, draw a straight line BC through O such that angle AOB is acute and angle AOC is obtuse. Label points B and C.

[Image: Line segment AO]

Figure, described in words:
A vertical line segment is drawn with a point at the top labeled with the letter "A" above it, and a point at the bottom labeled with the letter "O" below it.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: Through point O, draw a straight line BC that is slanted, not vertical. Place B on the upper-right ray from O, going up and to the right so that the angle AOB between OA (pointing up) and OB is acute, for example about 45°. Extend the line through O in the opposite direction, down and to the left, and place C there. Label B at the upper-right end and C at the lower-left end. Angle AOC is then the supplement of angle AOB, about 135°, which is obtuse.

llm_thinking:
I'm picturing AO as a vertical segment with A on top and O at the bottom, then drawing a second line through O so that angle AOB is acute — meaning B sits above O, tilted to one side within 90 degrees of OA.

Extending that same line past O in the opposite direction gives point C below and to the other side, making angle AOC the supplementary obtuse angle, roughly 135° if AOB is about 45°. So the answer is just a straight line through O crossing the vertical at an angle, with B and C labeled on opposite rays.
